priorInvolvementDisclosure: I authored the Claude 2 reviews of v2 (ACCEPT — wrong), v3, v5 and v7. v8 folds my three v7 findings, and CLAUDE-V8-S1 again concerns how the ledger records one of my own verdicts. blockers.title: basedOn.method drops the closed-roster completeness guarantee, and v8 then changes five paths outside its own roster
detail: v8's declared closed roster is seven entries: /artifact, /version, /date, /basedOn, /appliesFindingsOf, /honestyRepairsFromV7, /machineSurface/goldenShape/inputNotProduced. /reviewGuidance/forTheIndependentReviewer is not among them.

v8 nevertheless appends five entries to that path. The guidance array grows from 38 entries in v7 to 43 in v8. A recursive leaf-path diff of v7 against v8 returns 9 changed, 24 added and 1 removed, of which exactly five fall outside the declared roster — indices 38, 39, 40, 41 and 42 of /reviewGuidance/forTheIndependentReviewer. Every prior generation in this chain returned zero.

This is not an accident of wording. v7's method carried three clauses that v8 deletes: '/reviewGuidance/forTheIndependentReviewer (append)' as an explicit roster entry, 'honestyRepairsFromV1..V5 are historical', and the completeness guarantee 'Every path neither the roster nor succession metadata names is unchanged from v6.' v8's method has none of the three. With the completeness sentence gone there is no succession-metadata exemption to appeal to, and with the guidance path off the roster the appends are simply unaccounted.

The prior generations settle whether guidance appends need roster coverage: v5, v6 and v7 all placed '/reviewGuidance/forTheIndependentReviewer (append)' on the roster precisely so that appending there was declared. v8 kept the behaviour and dropped the declaration.

The five off-roster entries are, verbatim: 'Attack claude2v5 still missing ADV-SPC-V5-01..04.', 'Attack CLAUDE-V3-S1 written off as native/input work.', 'Attack a not-produced advertisement enum that still admits sarif.', 'Attack any silent v7-to-v8 path outside basedOn.method / honestyRepairsFromV7.', 'Do not mark DR-122 SATISFIED.' Entry 41 is the instruction to find this defect, and is itself one of the five instances of it.
blockers.whyBlockerGrade: Roster completeness is the one gate this chain has passed at every single generation — it is the mechanism that makes a successor auditable at all, and 'Silent-successor attack failed: every changed leaf is covered by the declared roster' appears in every frozen Codex verdict from v4 onward. v8 is the first generation to fail it, and it fails not through an overlooked edit but through the removal of the guarantee sentence that made the check meaningful. The content of the five appends is benign; the defect is that the artifact no longer states, and no longer satisfies, the property that its changes are exhaustively declared.
blockers.notAnAllegationOfConcealment: I make no claim that anything was hidden. The appends are visible, additive, and consistent with what a v8 should say. 'Silent' here is this chain's term of art for unrostered, not for covert.
blockers.minimumRepair: Restore the three deleted clauses to basedOn.method: add '/reviewGuidance/forTheIndependentReviewer (append)' to the closed roster, restore 'honestyRepairsFromV1..V6 are historical', and restore the completeness sentence in the form 'Every path neither the roster nor succession metadata names is unchanged from v7.' No byte of the appended guidance needs to change.

The frozen file at that digest, mode 0444, carries four: ADV-SPC-V7-01, ADV-SPC-V7-02, ADV-SPC-V7-03 and ADV-SPC-V7-04.

The sibling record in the same object does it correctly. claude2v5 lists all four of its ADV-SPC-V5-* identifiers, and notFoldedThisSuccessor carries a matching line for them. There is no equivalent line for the v7 advisories, so they are absent from the ledger in both places.
The omission is specific to claude2v7. codexv6 and codexv7 also omit the key, but I measured both frozen files and each genuinely carries zero advisories, so nothing is lost there.

CLAUDE-V7-B1 and Codex's SARIFV7-S1 were both, in substance, 'the ledger drops the advisories of a pinned frozen verdict'. v8 repairs that for the v5 verdict and reproduces it for the v7 verdict in the same commit.

A new pinChainRule member states 'Each successor pins the verdicts it folds. Earlier pins are recovered from the predecessor via basedOn.sha256. Immediate-predecessor pins for folded findings are retained on this ledger.' That is the general, mechanically recoverable rule both Codex's minimum repair and mine asked for, and it is what makes the absence of a codexv5 pin defensible rather than a silent drop.
The ledger also now carries four pins — claude2v5, codexv6, claude2v7, codexv7 — the most this chain has held, and both v7 reviewers are pinned at digests I re-measured and confirmed.

coordinatorNote: The design contract is finished work and should not be reopened: machineSurface is byte-identical to v7 apart from one enum narrowing, nativeMappings is byte-identical, and all five obligations pass. Both v7 reviewers' findings are genuinely discharged, including the pinChainRule that finally closes CLAUDE-V3-S1's class rather than its instance. A v9 needs only succession hygiene: restore the three clauses deleted from basedOn.method — the reviewGuidance roster entry, the historical-sections note, and the completeness sentence — and add the four ADV-SPC-V7-* identifiers to claude2v7 with a matching not-folded line. Neither repair touches a single byte of the projection law. Consider also extending pinChainRule to require that each pin record enumerate the full blocker, shouldFix and advisory roster of the file it pins; that would end a defect this chain has now hit at v3, v5, v7 and v8.

summary: REJECT at 1 blocker and 1 SHOULD-FIX, both in succession metadata rather than the projection law. Every folded v7 finding is genuinely repaired and I verified each against bytes: claude2v5 now carries all four ADV-SPC-V5-* identifiers that the frozen file actually contains and records them as not folded; CLAUDE-V3-S1 is restated as verdict-pin continuity, recorded OPEN, with CLAUDE-V3-B1/B2 correctly named as the native/input folds and a new pinChainRule supplying the mechanically recoverable predecessor rule both reviewers asked for; and inputNotProduced.advertisement is narrowed to ['none'], so the sarif+INACTIVE probe that passed v7's schema now fails it, with both preview fixtures still validating afterwards. All five obligations pass, machineSurface and nativeMappings are byte-identical to v7, both architecture pins reproduce at both HEADs, and the COORD pin remains an exact 218672-byte prefix. What fails is the succession guarantee itself: v8's basedOn.method deletes three clauses v7 carried — the /reviewGuidance/forTheIndependentReviewer (append) roster entry, the historical-sections note, and the completeness sentence 'Every path neither the roster nor succession metadata names is unchanged' — and v8 then appends five reviewGuidance entries, which a leaf-path diff shows are the first unrostered changes any generation of this chain has made. One of those five entries is the instruction to attack silent v7-to-v8 paths. Separately, the claude2v7 pin omits the four ADV-SPC-V7-* advisories its frozen file carries, reproducing for the v7 verdict the same ledger gap v8 just repaired for the v5 one.
